sentences: Continuous-variable quantum computation uses bosonic modes rather than a finite collection of two-level systems alone.
This source studies a model with cubic phase gates and proves an exponential-space upper bound on its computational power.
It asks whether that upper bound can be substantially improved, perhaps toward the classical counting classes that contain ordinary qubit quantum computation.
Cubic phase gates can rapidly increase the degree and coefficient size of operator expressions, obstructing straightforward simulations.
A tighter characterization would clarify which apparent extra power comes from the infinite-dimensional model and which reflects limitations of current analysis.
